source_caption:
The only actor in history to win three Oscar (Academy Awards) for Best Actor.

And this is one of the career-defining performance by Daniel Day-Lewis in There Will Be Blood (2007) who portrays a man who would rather lose his soul than his land. Watching Plainview a man of pure, unadulterated pride forced to scream his "sins" in front of a congregation just to secure a pipeline is one of the most uncomfortable and powerful moments in film history. 

Daniel Day-Lewis reportedly spent nearly two years preparing for his role as Daniel Plainview in the There Will Be Blood, immersing himself deeply in early 20th-century oil history. He studied letters and photographs of real oilmen to understand their behavior, developed Plainview’s harsh voice over months inspired partly by John Huston, learned old oilfield techniques, and stayed in character throughout filming. He also kept himself isolated to capture the character’s loneliness and intensity, a level of dedication that ultimately earned him his second Academy Award for Best Actor. 

Paul Dano, as Eli Sunday, is equally brilliant here perfectly matching Plainview’s intensity and turning their confrontation into one of the most electrifying acting duels ever put on screen.

source_details.synopsis: There Will Be Blood is a 2007 American epic period drama film co-produced, written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, loosely based on the 1927 novel Oil! by Upton Sinclair. It stars Daniel Day-Lewis, Paul Dano, Kevin J. O'Connor, Ciarán Hinds, and Dillon Freasier. The film follows silver miner-turned-oilman Daniel Plainview (Day-Lewis) as he embarks on a ruthless quest for wealth during the Californian oil boom in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It has often been considered as one of the greatest films of the 21st century and of all time.
